faq.compatibleQ: Will it work on my phone?
faq.compatibleA: Your phone must support eSIM and be carrier-unlocked. Most iPhones since the XS, Google Pixel 3 and later, and recent Samsung Galaxy models do.
faq.whenA: Install it before you leave, while you have Wi-Fi. The plan starts when it first connects at your destination, unless the plan says otherwise.
faq.numberQ: Do I keep my phone number?
faq.numberA: Yes. The eSIM is for data; your usual SIM stays in the phone for calls and texts.
faq.topupA: Plans marked "Top up this plan" or "Add more packages" can be topped up from My eSIMs.

copy.deviceChinaIphone: Most iPhones sold in mainland China, Hong Kong and Macao take two physical SIMs instead of an eSIM.
copy.deviceSamsung: Models sold in mainland China, Hong Kong, Taiwan and some US carrier models do not support eSIM.
copy.devicePixel3: Not the models sold in Australia, Taiwan or Japan, nor US models bought from carriers other than Sprint or Google Fi.
copy.faqWhatA: A SIM card built into your phone. You download a data plan by scanning a QR code — nothing to post, nothing to swap.
copy.faqStartA: Most plans start when the eSIM first connects at your destination, so you can install it days before you travel.
copy.faqNumberQ: Can I keep my own number for calls?

esim.searchPlans: Search name, destination or supplier plan id

esim.perDayNote: Prices are per day for this plan.
esim.previewSummary: {changed} of {considered} prices change: {up} up, {down} down ({avg}% on average); {active} of them are switched on.
esim.missingRates: No exchange rate for {currencies}: those plans keep their price.
esim.repriced: Saved. {count} plans re-priced; publish destinations to update the store.
esim.pricingHint: Selling price = cost × exchange rate × (1 + buffer) × (1 + markup), never below the minimum margin, rounded up. The most specific enabled rule sets the markup.
esim.minMarginHint: Of the selling price; protects against a low markup.
esim.fxBufferHint: Added to the converted cost against rate swings.
esim.threshold: Re-price when a rate moves more than %
esim.noRules: No rules: every plan uses the default markup.
esim.fxHint: European Central Bank rates, refreshed daily; latest {date}. A manual rate wins until removed.
esim.ruleHint: Leave a field on "any" to match everything. A rule naming more fields wins; between equals, the higher priority.
esim.syncStarted: Sync started. It can take a few minutes; refresh to see progress.
esim.providerPriority: Priority (lower is preferred when prices tie)
esim.providersHint: The eSIM suppliers plans are bought from. A supplier that is off is neither synced nor sold.
esim.confirmCancel: Cancel this eSIM at the supplier? It stops working; refund the shopper separately if needed.
esim.notResent: The email could not be sent; check the order's email address and the mail settings
esim.redacted: Keys, passwords and activation codes are removed before a call is stored.
esim.problemsHint: eSIMs that could not be issued, or are taking too long. A failed eSIM of a registered shopper is refunded to store credit on its own; a guest's needs a refund by hand.
esim.noProblems: Nothing needs a person right now.
esim.mayStillDeliver: The supplier may still have issued this eSIM. Check its portal before trying another supplier or refunding.
esim.bind: Bind an eSIM bought by hand
esim.confirmFail: Stop trying and refund the shopper (store credit; a guest needs a refund by hand)?
esim.bindHint: The eSIM is read from the chosen supplier by its ICCID, recorded on the order and emailed to the shopper.
esim.bound: eSIM bound and sent to the shopper
esim.confirmPlansOff: Switch off every plan of {count} destinations? They leave the store at the next publish.
esim.confirmPublishDestinations: Publish {count} destinations? New products are created as drafts.
esim.searchDestinations: Country, region or a covered country
esim.devicesBuiltIn: The store shows the built-in list of {count} models. Import it to change it, or add models one by one.
esim.devicesHint: The phones and tablets the device check on the store knows.
esim.noDevices: No models in the list yet.
esim.jobFulfilment: Retries, supplier polls and paid orders never queued. Every minute.
esim.jobCatalog: Syncs every active supplier's plans. Every 6 hours.
esim.jobFx: Loads the day's exchange rates and re-prices plans whose currency moved. Daily.
esim.jobStarted: Started. Refresh in a moment to see the result.
esim.jobsHint: They run when the scheduler calls their address with CRON_SECRET: on Vercel from vercel.json, on your own server from its cron.
esim.jobsStale: A job has not run on schedule. Without the fulfilment job, retries and slow suppliers are never picked up again.
esim.mappingHint: The first plan of each variant is the primary: the variant sells at its price and is bought from it first; the others are tried in order if it refuses. The cheapest leads unless you pin one.
esim.notPublishedYet: Not published yet: switch plans on and publish the destination from the plan library.
esim.helpPagesHint: Ready-made pages built from the eSIM blocks; edit them in the page builder and link them from your menus.
esim.topupsHint: Data top-ups shoppers bought for their eSIMs. A failed top-up is refunded to the shopper's store credit on its own.
esim.noTopupProblems: No top-up needs a person right now.
esim.topupMayHaveHappened: The supplier may already have made this top-up. Check its portal before refunding; trying again is safe.
esim.confirmFailTopup: Stop trying and refund the shopper's store credit?
esim.jobUsage: Checks live eSIMs' usage with their suppliers, sends shopper reminders and pays referral rewards that are due. Every 30 minutes.
esim.remindersHint: Sent by the usage job by email, and in the account for registered shoppers: when the eSIM connects, when data runs low (with a top-up link), before the plan ends and before the install-by date. Each is sent once.
esim.walletHint: Shoppers add money to their balance from My eSIMs and pay for it at checkout. The amount is booked as balance owed to them, the fee as income; balance added this way is not refunded as money.
esim.referralsHint: Shoppers share /esim/invite/[code]. A friend who opens an account through it earns them a reward on each order delivered, added to their balance after the holding period — booked as a promotion. {count} shoppers have joined through a referral.
esim.referralCouponHint: A one-use coupon for their account only, made when they sign up through a link.
esim.kycHint: Shoppers verify their identity once, in My eSIMs. A plan that needs it can then be checked out only by a verified shopper, and never by a guest.
esim.kycFormHint: Publishing makes a new version; submissions keep the version they answered.
esim.kycRulesHint: A plan needs KYC when it is set so in the plan library; otherwise when it covers a listed country; otherwise when its supplier says so. Set in the plan library: {required} need it, {notRequired} do not.
esim.confirmKyc: Change whether {count} plans need identity verification?
esim.kycNoStorage: File storage is not set up (Settings → Storage), so shoppers cannot upload documents. Set it up, or publish a form without file questions.
esim.paymentsHint: Payments made with the eSIM payment gateways. The order is placed when the gateway confirms the payment; refunds of these payments are made by hand in the gateway.
esim.payStripeHint: In the Stripe Dashboard, add this notification URL as a webhook endpoint for checkout.session.completed, checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded, checkout.session.async_payment_failed, checkout.session.expired, and paste its signing secret (whsec_…) into webhookSecret. methods is optional, e.g. alipay,wechat_pay; left empty, Stripe offers the payment methods switched on in its Dashboard.
esim.checkoutDisplayHint: The order shoppers see the payment methods in, the one chosen when checkout opens, and each one's icon. Only methods switched on are shown. The account balance always comes first when it covers the order.
esim.checkoutNoDefault: No default: the first one that can take the order
esim.esimGatewaysHint: Gateways run by the eSIM module. Each one switched on and set up is a payment method of its own at checkout; the order is placed when the gateway confirms the payment, and refunds are made by hand in the gateway.
esim.paymentsMoved: The gateways, their order and icons at checkout, and the payment fees are set under Settings → Payment.
esim.payOutcomeClosed: Checkout had closed — send it back
esim.payConfirmRefunded: Record that {amount} was sent back to the shopper through {method}?
esim.migConfirm: Import the old store's shoppers, balances, referrals and active eSIMs now? Shoppers are not emailed. Running it again later only adds what is new.
esim.migStarted: Started; this page updates when it is done
esim.migHint: Brings shoppers (with their old passwords), balances, referrals and active eSIMs over from the old store. Old orders are not imported. Sync every supplier's catalogue first: an eSIM whose plan is not here yet is left out, and the next import picks it up.
esim.migNoSource: Not configured — set LEGACY_MYSQL_HOST, LEGACY_MYSQL_DATABASE, LEGACY_MYSQL_USER and LEGACY_MYSQL_PASSWORD in .env and restart.
esim.cancelHint: A shopper can cancel an eSIM not installed yet, on a plan its supplier marks refundable, when the supplier cancels through its API. The supplier is asked first; the shopper is refunded only once it agrees.
esim.reportsHint: eSIM sales and gross margin at the prices and supplier costs recorded when each eSIM was bought. Amounts in USD; days in UTC.
esim.reportMarginNote: {percent} of sales with a known cost
esim.reportCostUnknown: {count} sales have no supplier cost in USD (no exchange rate at the time) and are left out of the margin.
esim.reportNoSnapshot: {count} eSIMs issued in this range were bought before sale records were kept, or imported, and are not counted.
esim.reportVoided: {count} eSIMs ({amount}) were cancelled or refunded and are not counted as sales.
esim.confirmApprove: Buy every eSIM of this order now?
esim.confirmReject: Buy nothing for this order? Then refund the payment in Storify (Orders → Refund) to where it came from.
esim.approvedDone: Approved; the eSIMs are being bought
esim.rejectedDone: Rejected; refund the payment in Storify
esim.riskHint: Hold a paid order's eSIMs for a person before anything is bought from a supplier. Held orders appear under eSIM → Problems, to approve or reject. 0 turns a rule off.
esim.riskOrders: Review once a buyer already has this many orders
esim.campaignsHint: A campaign is a page with a banner and a coupon code for chosen destinations, for its dates. The code is a Storify coupon kept in step with the campaign, and works only on those destinations' eSIMs.
esim.campaignConfirmDelete: Remove this campaign? Its page goes, and its coupon code stops working.
esim.campaignActive: Active: the page and the code work between the dates
esim.feesHint: Added to an order for the way it is paid: a fixed amount plus a percent of the goods, shown at checkout as a "Payment fee" line and refunded with the order. Paying from the balance, and wallet top-ups, carry no fee.
esim.balanceHoldHint: Every supplier for this eSIM is out of balance. Top one up: it is tried again every 10 minutes (or retry it now) until {until}, then refunded.
esim.navHint: The bar at the bottom of the store on phones and tablets. Turn tabs on or off, put them in order and rename them. At most {max} show; Menu always stays, as it is the only way into the side menu on a phone.
esim.navCustom: The store shows the bar set here.
esim.navDefault: The store shows its own bar. Save to use the one set here.
esim.navRestored: The store's own bar is back
esim.menuHint: The menu the Menu tab opens on phones and tablets. Hide the parts you do not need, and list eSIM pages or your own links under Home. The links in the middle still come from the header menu under Online store → Navigation.
esim.numbersOnlySupplier: Number cards (stock imported under eSIM → Numbers)
esim.numbersHint: TopConnect number cards held as stock. {available} free · {reserved} held · {sold} sold · {retired} off sale
esim.searchNumbers: Number, ICCID, batch or customer email
esim.importNumbersHint: One card per line, as TopConnect sends them: MSISDN ICCID LPA PIN1 PUK1 PIN2 PUK2, separated by spaces, tabs or commas. A line may end with its own price and premium. Numbers already in stock are skipped.
esim.dialCodeHint: Leave the country code empty when every number already starts with its own.
esim.numbersCheckResult: {imported} would be imported · {existing} already in stock · {problems} lines with problems
esim.numbersImportResult: {imported} imported · {existing} already in stock · {problems} lines with problems
esim.numberPackagesHint: Data packets a number owner can buy. The cost is TopConnect's price, moved onto the card before the packet is switched on; the price follows the pricing rules unless you set it.
esim.loadPacketsNeeds: Needs the TopConnect supplier switched on and a number in stock
esim.noPackets: No data packages yet. Load them from TopConnect or add one by hand.
esim.packetIdHint: The packet ID is TopConnect's packet code, the one switched on for the card.
esim.packetCountriesHint: Countries where it works (codes, e.g. FR, DE, IT)
esim.numberProductProblem: Numbers cannot be bought yet: the store product they are sold as could not be made ({reason}).
esim.numberSettingsHint: Every number is sold with a first recharge. The smallest recharge applies to that first one and to later ones: whole amounts in the card's currency ({currency}).
esim.providerCurrencyHint: Costs without a currency of their own are read in this currency and converted to USD at the exchange rate plus the buffer.
esim.providerCurrencyInvalid: Enter a three-letter currency code, such as USD or EUR
esim.packetLoadHint: TopConnect lists the packages of the network a card is on. A card not in use is on no network, so enter the network code (MCC+MNC) of a network the packages are for, e.g. 24801. The code entered is remembered.
esim.destinationNamesHint: The supplier calls it "{name}". Leave a language empty to show the automatic name in grey: the country's own name for a single country, the supplier's name otherwise.
esim.mergeHint: For two destinations that are the same place under different supplier names. This destination's plans, and any the suppliers add later, are then sold under the one you pick, and this page's address redirects there. Destinations of a single country are merged automatically.
esim.mergeConfirm: Merge "{from}" into "{into}"? Its product goes to draft and its address redirects there.
esim.unmerged: Merge undone. That destination's product stays in draft until you show it again.
